brief.topic: Human-in-the-loop is a dial, not a switch
brief.audience: PMs designing review steps for AI features

coreInsight: Human review has levels — review all, review risky, sample, audit — and you set the level per task, moving down only when reviewers rarely change the AI’s output.

hooks.text: Human review is a dial, not a switch.
hooks.notes: Replaces the on/off debate with a clear model the reel then lays out.

caption.opening: “Keep a human in the loop” is where the design starts, not where it ends.
body:
Four settings for human review:
→ Review all: a person approves every output
→ Review risky: only flagged or high-stakes cases
→ Sample: check a random slice each week
→ Audit: look at logs after incidents
The metric that moves the dial: how often reviewers change what the AI produced. When that stays low on a task, move that task down one level. When it rises, move it back up.
Set it per task. A refund promise and a greeting don’t deserve the same review.
